@acetcom 

## Test Environment
Built and tested `open5gs:main` with version `Open5GS v2.7.6-188-gebc6694`.

## Reproduction Result
The system still eventually hit the following crash:
`amf FATAL: ogs_sbi_subscription_data_add: Assertion 'subscription_data' failed.`

### AMF log (crash point)
```log
03/10 20:16:45.810: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_sbi_subscription_data_add: Assertion `subscription_data' failed. (../lib/sbi/context.c:2758)
03/10 20:16:45.811: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_sbi_subscription_data_add+0x149) [0x7f0fc3353c29]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_nnrf_nfm_send_nf_status_subscribe+0xa7) [0x7f0fc3363a20]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_sbi_nf_state_registered+0x361) [0x7f0fc336aaf1]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x223d2) [0x7f0fc38713d2]

./open5gs-amfd(+0x4be51) [0x55e547fd0e51]

./open5gs-amfd(+0xba4d) [0x55e547f90a4d]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x12b4f) [0x7f0fc3861b4f]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3) [0x7f0fc2a16ac3]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44) [0x7f0fc2aa7a84]
Open5GS daemon v2.7.6-188-gebc6694
```
### Extra suspicious log on AMF side
```log
03/10 19:04:27.990: [sbi] DEBUG: [d5dec9e4-1c83-41f1-9372-65d253c533ea] Skip subscription delete: DELETE already sent (../lib/sbi/context.c:2895)
```
## Observed Timeline
- Open5GS started at `03/10 13:19:57.955`
- AMF connected to the gNB at `03/10 14:15:34.274`
- The first `No Heartbeat` occurred at `03/10 14:20:07.520`
- This was followed by `Sending NRF subscription DELETE before NF re-registration`
- A large number of `Skip subscription delete: DELETE already sent` logs began appearing around `03/10 19:04:27`
- The AMF finally crashed at `03/10 20:16:45.810`

## Question
Under this condition, if heartbeat is set to `0`, would NF-to-NRF communication still work normally, or would that introduce any side effects or other issues?

@anna092 

Thanks for the report.

I looked into the issue and applied an additional fix to the main branch.  
The changes address two points:

1) Prevent duplicate NF status subscriptions from being created during
   repeated re-registration cycles.

2) Ensure the local subscription_data entry is cleaned up after receiving
   the DELETE response, even when the HTTP status is not 204.

This should prevent stale subscription_data entries from accumulating
and eventually exhausting the pool.

Please take a look when you have time and let me know if you still see
the issue.

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan
